biography.plain_text: Owen Perry is an American hotelier, developer and co-founder of The Villa Group. long_biography.plain_text:
The Villa Group grew from a decision by Owen Perry, Luz María Torres and Fernando Gonzalez to leave a timeshare employer and establish their own resort business. The partners paired vacation ownership with hotel operations and in-house construction, allowing them to select coastal sites, build the properties and retain control of the guest product. Their first Puerto Vallarta projects became the base for expansion along Mexico's Pacific coast and into Cancún.

In Loreto, Perry applied the same integrated model to a destination built around a Villa del Palmar resort, residential development and a golf course designed by Rees Jones. The PGA Tour's TPC Network then designated the Rees Jones course as a TPC property.

uncertainties.detail: Several people named Owen Perry appear online. The exact identity clears the threshold because the immutable Danzante Bay developer anchor matches the distinctive Villa Group, Loreto, TPC and Rancho Santa Fe combination across official and independent sources. Unrelated namesakes were excluded.
Reliable sources variously place The Villa Group's beginning in 1983, 1984 or 1985. The dossier uses the durable mid-1980s sequence and does not state an exact founding year in either biography.

The move from timeshare employment to a separately founded resort business establishes a founder-built, non-inherited core asset. Perry's earlier family wealth, education and launch capital are not documented well enough to choose Self-made — independent start or Self-made — advantaged start, so the broader Self-made value is used.

The Villa Group combines hotels, vacation ownership, residences, construction and property sales. Hospitality is used for both industry fields because the resorts and guest operations are the durable core platform; property development is described as an integrated activity rather than classified separately.

No strong public source reviewed establishes Perry's birth day, month, year or place. The existing American nationality and United States birth country remain unchanged, and no birth-detail proposal is made.

The source biography is narrowly focused on an ownership-identification chain. To keep this dossier free of vessel content, it is not duplicated as a correction baseline or proposed for direct overwrite; the new short and long biographies remain available in the research metadata.

No dedicated Forbes profile, verified Instagram, Facebook, X, YouTube, TikTok or personal website was found. The exact LinkedIn and official Villa Group domain cleared the threshold; same-name accounts did not.
Current vessel facts, current resort prices and awards, private family details and volatile property or project values were excluded. Nothing has been compiled or applied.
